member.name: T:IntomicLib.ConcurrentExclusiveLock
member.summary: Provides a high-performance, non-recursive synchronization lock based on Concurrent / Exclusive access permissions.
member.remarks:
This lock represents access permissions rather than read/write intent. Concurrent means that the current operation may enter alongside other Concurrent operations; Exclusive means that the current operation must enter exclusively and cannot run concurrently with any other operation. This lock does not provide recursive nesting privileges.
This lock supports preemptive Exclusive access, in-place upgrade from Concurrent to Exclusive, in-place downgrade from Exclusive to Concurrent, and observation snapshots for state and contention.
Ordinary Concurrent acquisition and release primarily use lightweight atomic counting and do not enter the Monitor scheduling queue. Ordinary Exclusive acquisition, and conversion from Concurrent to Exclusive through an in-place upgrade, use Monitor's mutual exclusion, waiting, signaling, and scheduling mechanisms for exclusive coordination.
This lock does not guarantee strict FIFO ordering and does not promise stronger scheduling fairness than Monitor. Actual thread execution order remains affected by operating-system scheduling, CPU topology, cache state, system load, and the duration of caller workloads.
This type is intended for synchronous, non-recursive, highly concurrent shared-state scenarios, especially server-side systems containing large numbers of fine-grained lock objects.
This type is a value type, and a default-initialized instance is unusable. Use to create an instance.

member.name: P:IntomicLib.ConcurrentExclusiveLock.ObservedState
member.summary: An observation snapshot of the lock's current state.
member.remarks:
This value only represents the lock state observed at the instant of the read. It must not be used as an exact lock-state test and is intended only for diagnostics and monitoring.
After a preemptive Exclusive request enters the contention window, this value may already be observed as Exclusive even while the request is still waiting for current Concurrent holders to release.
Therefore, ObservedState represents the lock's current access tendency or transition state; it does not mean that a thread is already executing Exclusive-protected application code.

member.summary: Atomically gets or sets the business context ID associated with the current lock.
member.remarks:
This property records additional application state outside the lock protocol, such as the current context identified by the application layer, allowing the same context to be recognized and duplicate permission acquisition to be avoided.
Setting this property directly overwrites the current ContextID unconditionally. To determine whether the context actually changes, use .
A value of 0 means that no context ID is set. The meaning, allocation, validation, and cleanup of nonzero values are the caller's responsibility.

member.name: M:IntomicLib.ConcurrentExclusiveLock.TryAcquireConcurrent(System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Attempts to acquire Concurrent access permission within the specified time.
member.remarks:
This method waits, for up to the specified timeout, for the lock to enter a state in which Concurrent permission can be acquired.
A nonzero return value means that Concurrent permission was acquired. The caller may later call ReleaseConcurrent() to release it manually. If the held state is subsequently converted through another protocol operation, release it according to the converted state. When is 0, the method performs a single attempt without waiting; a value less than 0 means an infinite wait. limits the maximum Concurrent ID permitted for this acquisition. must not be less than 1. When is greater than or equal to 0, the method waits at most until the timeout expires and then returns 0; when is less than 0, the method waits indefinitely.
member.param: The maximum number of milliseconds to wait for Concurrent permission. 0 performs a single attempt without waiting; a value less than 0 means an infinite wait.
The maximum permitted Concurrent ID. A successful return value is in the range [1, maxConcurrent].
member.returns: The Concurrent ID acquired by this operation, in the range [1, maxConcurrent]; 0 if Concurrent permission was not acquired within the specified time.

member.name: M:IntomicLib.ConcurrentExclusiveLock.AcquireExclusive
member.summary: Waits to acquire Exclusive access permission.
member.remarks:
This method requests preemptive Exclusive permission.
Once the request is issued, the lock blocks new Concurrent entries and waits for current Concurrent holders to release. The method returns after the lock enters the Exclusive state.
After acquiring Exclusive permission, the caller may later call ReleaseExclusive() to release it manually, or call ExclusiveToConcurrent() to downgrade to Concurrent and then release according to the Concurrent protocol.

member.name: M:IntomicLib.ConcurrentExclusiveLock.TryAcquireExclusive(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Attempts to acquire Exclusive access permission.
member.remarks:
When is true, this method requests Exclusive permission preemptively. If Concurrent holders currently exist, the lock blocks new Concurrent entries and participates in exclusive contention; a successful Exclusive request waits for current Concurrent holders to release before acquiring Exclusive permission.
When is false, this method does not preempt Concurrent holders. It returns false immediately whenever Concurrent or Exclusive permission is currently held.
A return value of true means that Exclusive permission was acquired. The caller may later call ReleaseExclusive() to release it manually, or call ExclusiveToConcurrent() to downgrade to Concurrent and then release according to the Concurrent protocol.
A return value of false means that Exclusive permission was not acquired, and the caller must not execute application code that depends on Exclusive permission.
member.param: true to allow preemption of Concurrent holders; false to avoid preemption, in which case Exclusive permission can be acquired only when the lock is Idle.
member.returns: true if Exclusive permission was acquired; otherwise, false.

member.remarks:
This method attempts to acquire preemptive Exclusive permission within the specified timeout. When is 0, the method performs a single attempt without waiting; a value less than 0 means an infinite wait.

A return value of false means that Exclusive permission was not acquired within the specified time, and the caller must not execute application code that depends on Exclusive permission.

member.name: M:IntomicLib.ConcurrentExclusiveLock.ReleaseExclusive
member.summary: Releases the currently held Exclusive access permission.
member.remarks:
This method must be called in a context where the current scope holds Exclusive permission.
After the call, the current scope no longer holds Exclusive permission and must not continue executing application code that depends on it.
After release completes, the lock returns to normal contention, and waiting Concurrent or Exclusive requests continue attempting to enter according to the lock's contention rules.
To retain Concurrent permission after finishing the Exclusive region, call ExclusiveToConcurrent() instead of this method.

member.name: M:IntomicLib.ConcurrentExclusiveLock.ExclusiveToConcurrent
member.summary: Downgrades the currently held Exclusive access permission to Concurrent access permission.
member.remarks:
This method must be called in a context where the current scope holds Exclusive permission.
After the call, the current scope no longer holds Exclusive permission and must not continue executing application code that depends on it.
The current scope continues to hold Concurrent permission and may later call ReleaseConcurrent() to release it manually.
This method preserves a continuous Concurrent access context after exclusive modification, avoiding the access window created by releasing Exclusive and then reacquiring Concurrent.

member.name: M:IntomicLib.ConcurrentExclusiveLock.TryConcurrentToExclusiveWithSwitchContextID(System.Int32)
member.summary: While holding Concurrent permission, attempts to upgrade the current permission to Exclusive through SwitchContextID. When multiple Concurrent holders call this method simultaneously with the same newContextID, only the holder that successfully switches ContextID can upgrade. When callers use different newContextID values, multiple callers may each succeed, but their successful Exclusive regions are still isolated and ordered. After a successful upgrade, the current scope holds Exclusive permission; after a failed upgrade, the current scope's Concurrent permission is released automatically.
member.remarks:
This method must be called in a context where the current scope holds Concurrent permission.
After the call, the lock blocks new Concurrent entries into the current conversion window, and a caller that successfully upgrades executes in isolation under Exclusive semantics. Whether ContextID is switched successfully is determined by SwitchContextID(newContextID).
After success, the caller may call ReleaseExclusive() to release it manually. After failure, the original Concurrent permission has already been released and the caller must not call ReleaseConcurrent().

member.name: M:IntomicLib.ConcurrentExclusiveLock.TryConcurrentToExclusiveWithRaiseEpochID(System.Int32)
member.summary: While holding Concurrent permission, attempts to upgrade the current permission to Exclusive through RaiseEpochID. The caller can advance the epoch and upgrade successfully only when newEpochID is greater than the current EpochID. When newEpochID is less than or equal to the current EpochID, the upgrade fails and EpochID remains unchanged. When multiple callers use different, increasing newEpochID values, multiple callers may each succeed, but their successful Exclusive regions are still isolated and ordered. After a successful upgrade, the current scope holds Exclusive permission; after a failed upgrade, the current scope's Concurrent permission is released automatically.
member.remarks:
This method must be called in a context where the current scope holds Concurrent permission.
This method is suitable when EpochID represents a lifecycle, version number, or phase number. EpochID may only advance to a greater value; it cannot remain unchanged or move backward. After the call, the lock blocks new Concurrent entries into the current conversion window, and a caller that successfully upgrades executes in isolation under Exclusive semantics.
After success, the caller may call ReleaseExclusive() to release it manually. After failure, the original Concurrent permission has already been released and the caller must not call ReleaseConcurrent().

member.name: T:IntomicLib.ConcurrentExclusiveLockPipeline
member.summary: An access-permission Pipeline for .
member.remarks:
A Pipeline describes an application workflow as a sequence of segments, each declaring the access permission it requires. During execution, the Pipeline automatically releases, reacquires, or converts permissions in place according to the permission successfully held by the previous segment.
Concurrent represents an independent ordinary Concurrent permission segment; consecutive ordinary Concurrent segments are separated and reacquired. ConvergeConcurrent preserves or establishes a Concurrent context; if the previous segment held Exclusive permission, it is downgraded to Concurrent in place.
TryApplyIDConvergeExclusive first attempts to apply a business ID and, on success, converges to Exclusive: if the previous segment held Concurrent permission, the corresponding in-place upgrade method is called according to the ID type; if the previous segment held Exclusive permission, the business ID is applied within the current Exclusive context; if no permission is currently held, the business ID is applied first and Exclusive permission is acquired after success.
An Exclusive segment reacquires an independent Exclusive permission; even when the previous segment already held Exclusive permission, it is released and reacquired so that other contenders have an opportunity to enter. To continue execution within an existing Exclusive context under business-ID control, use TryApplyIDConvergeExclusive.
When TryConcurrent, TestExclusive, TryExclusive, or TryApplyIDConvergeExclusive does not satisfy its target execution condition, the current segment is skipped; the Pipeline neither throws nor terminates, and instead continues interpreting subsequent segments from the None state.

member.summary: Executes a sequence of Pipeline segments in order.
member.remarks: Each segment declares the access permission it requires, and the Pipeline automatically selects the appropriate operation according to the permission successfully held by the previous segment. Ordinary and represent independent permission segments; even when the previous segment holds the same kind of permission, it is released and reacquired. preserves or establishes a Concurrent context; if the previous segment holds Exclusive permission, it is downgraded to Concurrent in place. has Try semantics for updating the business ID. member.summary: Attempts to acquire Exclusive permission only when the lock is Idle.

member.summary: Preemptively attempts to acquire Exclusive permission.
member.remarks: This mode may block new Concurrent entries while attempting to acquire Exclusive permission. If Exclusive permission is not acquired, the current segment is skipped and the Pipeline continues from the None state. member.name: F:IntomicLib.ConcurrentExclusiveAccessMode.ConvergeConcurrent
member.summary: Preserves or acquires Concurrent permission.
member.remarks: If the previous segment already holds Concurrent permission, the current Concurrent context is preserved and the segment executes directly. If the previous segment holds Exclusive permission, ExclusiveToConcurrent() is called to downgrade it in place before the segment executes. If no permission is currently held, ordinary Concurrent permission is acquired.

member.name: F:IntomicLib.ConcurrentExclusiveAccessMode.TryApplyIDConvergeExclusive
member.summary: Attempts to apply a business ID and, on success, converge to Exclusive permission.
member.remarks:
The Try semantics of this mode apply to updating the business ID, not to acquiring Exclusive permission.
If Concurrent permission is currently held, an in-place upgrade is performed according to the segment's IDType: with ContextID, TryConcurrentToExclusiveWithSwitchContextID(contextID) is called; with EpochID, TryConcurrentToExclusiveWithRaiseEpochID(epochID) is called.
If Exclusive permission is already held, the business ID declared by the current segment is applied: with ContextID, SwitchContextID(contextID) is called; with EpochID, RaiseEpochID(epochID) is called.
If no access permission is currently held, the declared business ID is applied first; after the ID is applied successfully, the Pipeline waits for and acquires Exclusive permission.
The current segment executes only when the business ID is applied successfully and the Pipeline ultimately enters or retains Exclusive permission. If applying the business ID fails, the current segment is skipped; the Pipeline releases any permission it still holds and continues interpreting subsequent segments from the None state.

member.remarks:

A Scope instance is intended for a single execution context, does not support concurrent operations from multiple threads, and must not be copied.

member.summary: Attempts to acquire Exclusive access permission.
member.remarks:
When is true, this method requests Exclusive permission preemptively. If Concurrent holders currently exist, the lock blocks new Concurrent entries and participates in exclusive contention; a successful Exclusive request waits for current Concurrent holders to release before acquiring Exclusive permission.
When is false, this method does not preempt Concurrent holders. It returns false immediately whenever Concurrent or Exclusive permission is currently held.
A return value of true means that Exclusive permission was acquired. The caller may later call ReleaseExclusive() to release it manually, or call ExclusiveToConcurrent() to downgrade to Concurrent and then release according to the Concurrent protocol. If it is not released manually, releases it according to the final state held by the scope.
A return value of false means that Exclusive permission was not acquired, and the caller must not execute application code that depends on Exclusive permission.
member.param: true to allow preemption of Concurrent holders; false to avoid preemption, in which case Exclusive permission can be acquired only when the lock is Idle.
member.returns: true if Exclusive permission was acquired; otherwise, false.

member.name: M:IntomicLib.ConcurrentExclusiveLockScope.ReleaseExclusive
member.summary: Releases the currently held Exclusive access permission.
member.remarks:
This method must be called in a context where the current scope holds Exclusive permission.
After the call, the current scope no longer holds Exclusive permission and must not continue executing application code that depends on it.
After release completes, the lock returns to normal contention, and waiting Concurrent or Exclusive requests continue attempting to enter according to the lock's contention rules.
To retain Concurrent permission after finishing the Exclusive region, call ExclusiveToConcurrent() instead of this method.

member.name: M:IntomicLib.ConcurrentExclusiveLockScope.ExclusiveToConcurrent
member.summary: Downgrades the currently held Exclusive access permission to Concurrent access permission.
member.remarks:
This method must be called in a context where the current scope holds Exclusive permission.
After the call, the current scope no longer holds Exclusive permission and must not continue executing application code that depends on it.
The current scope continues to hold Concurrent permission and may later call ReleaseConcurrent() to release it manually. If it is not released manually, releases it according to the final state held by the scope.
This method preserves a continuous Concurrent access context after exclusive modification, avoiding the access window created by releasing Exclusive and then reacquiring Concurrent.

member.name: M:IntomicLib.ConcurrentExclusiveLockScope.TryConcurrentToExclusiveWithSwitchContextID(System.Int32)
member.summary: While holding Concurrent permission, attempts to upgrade the current permission to Exclusive through SwitchContextID. When multiple Concurrent holders call this method simultaneously with the same newContextID, only the holder that successfully switches ContextID can upgrade. When callers use different newContextID values, multiple callers may each succeed, but their successful Exclusive regions are still isolated and ordered. After a successful upgrade, the current scope holds Exclusive permission; after a failed upgrade, the current scope's Concurrent permission is released automatically.
member.remarks:
This method must be called in a context where the current scope holds Concurrent permission.
After the call, the lock blocks new Concurrent entries into the current conversion window, and a caller that successfully upgrades executes in isolation under Exclusive semantics. Whether ContextID is switched successfully is determined by SwitchContextID(newContextID).
After success, the caller may call ReleaseExclusive() to release it manually. If it is not released manually, releases it according to the final state held by the scope.
After failure, the original Concurrent permission has already been released and the caller must not call ReleaseConcurrent().

member.name: M:IntomicLib.ConcurrentExclusiveLockScope.TryConcurrentToExclusiveWithRaiseEpochID(System.Int32)
member.summary: While holding Concurrent permission, attempts to upgrade the current permission to Exclusive through RaiseEpochID. The caller can advance the epoch and upgrade successfully only when newEpochID is greater than the current EpochID. When newEpochID is less than or equal to the current EpochID, the upgrade fails and EpochID remains unchanged. When multiple callers use different, increasing newEpochID values, multiple callers may each succeed, but their successful Exclusive regions are still isolated and ordered. After a successful upgrade, the current scope holds Exclusive permission; after a failed upgrade, the current scope's Concurrent permission is released automatically.
member.remarks:
This method must be called in a context where the current scope holds Concurrent permission.
This method is suitable when EpochID represents a lifecycle, version number, or phase number. EpochID may only advance to a greater value; it cannot remain unchanged or move backward. After the call, the lock blocks new Concurrent entries into the current conversion window, and a caller that successfully upgrades executes in isolation under Exclusive semantics.
After success, the caller may call ReleaseExclusive() to release it manually. If it is not released manually, releases it according to the final state held by the scope.
After failure, the original Concurrent permission has already been released and the caller must not call ReleaseConcurrent().
